Day two of the Digital Skills for the Future Summit is underway in Boksburg, Gauteng.

Today’s programme focuses on a full day of commissions, bringing stakeholders together to engage on key areas of digital skills development in South Africa. These include Foundational Digital Skills: C&R and DT, which focuses on building essential digital literacy and technology skills; Computer Applications Technology (CAT), which explores the use of computer applications and digital tools in learning; Information Technology (IT), which looks at computing, programming and technical skills; eLearning, which focuses on using digital platforms and resources to support teaching and learning; ICT Infrastructure & System Support, which addresses connectivity, infrastructure and the systems needed to enable digital learning; and AI Guidelines, which considers the responsible and effective use of artificial intelligence in education.

The various commissions will present their feedback and recommendations during tomorrow’s final day of the summit.

tweets.text:
I’m not so worried about artificial intelligence.
I’m more worried about natural stupidity.

Not because people are unintelligent. But because we are all vulnerable to the same trap: Confirmation bias.

We look for evidence that proves we're right and ignore evidence that suggests we're wrong.

Science taught me that progress starts with a simple sentence: "I might be wrong."

The most important skill in the AI era won't be coding.
It won't be prompting.
It will be critical thinking.

The ability to change your mind when the evidence changes. And artificial intelligence is getting smarter every year.

My hope is that we use that intelligence, and all the new knowledge it unlocks, not to create more division, conflict, and war...

...but to better understand one another, solve our biggest challenges, and build a more peaceful world.

Because the real question isn't whether machines will become smarter.

It's whether humanity will become wiser...
